title: DX Quality Radar: Initiative to standardize SDKs, docs, and quickstarts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Build a repeatable 'Quality Radar' gating and tracking system for all Developer Experience surface area (official SDKs, core docs, and quickstarts). The Radar establishes objective checks, telemetry signals, and release gates so every DX artifact shipped meets baseline reliability, example parity, and onboarding speed goals. Goals: 1) Define a minimal, machine-checkable spec for SDKs, docs, and quickstarts (linting, CI, smoke tests, example coverage). 2) Instrument onboarding telemetry so we can measure 'time-to-first-successful-call' and first-week retention per SDK/guide. 3) Integrate Radar checks into the release flow (PR -> CI -> Radar pass required) and track radar health on Console and internal dashboards. Deliverables: - Quality Radar spec document (markdown) with checks and severity levels. - CI templates and GitHub Actions for SDKs and quickstarts. - Two end-to-end smoke test suites (JS SDK + Python SDK) ran in CI and Canary. - Quickstart harvest dashboard in Metabase with onboarding funnel and NPS feedback link. - Rollout plan and enforcement policy (soft-block -> hard-block cadence). Why this now: We continue to see regressions and user confusion caused by mismatched examples, drift between SDKs and API surface, and variable quickstart completion rates. A lightweight gating layer reduces regressions, accelerates onboarding improvements, and provides data-backed prioritization for engineering and docs work.
acceptance_criteria: Published Quality Radar spec in the Developer Experience handbook with owner and severity mapping

At least two repos enforcing Radar checks in 'soft-block' mode for one sprint with no false-positives above tolerance
Onboarding funnel dashboard shows baseline and daily delta; alerts defined for regressions >15% week-over-week

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Excessive false positives from strict checks could slow down contributors. Mitigation: start with soft-block and maintain an exceptions list; provide clear remediation guidance.
Risk: Telemetry privacy/compliance concerns for quickstarts. Mitigation: only record anonymized success events; consult Security for PII-safe schema.
Risk: Resource contention with runtime team for E2E tests. Mitigation: use small mocked endpoints and budget nightly GPU time for integration runs.
